the use of the 2015 WHO classification of pancreatic cancer, based on the molecular genetic characteristics of the tumor, is associated with improved prognostication of survival and recurrence in patients with resectable pancreatic cancer.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current data are insufficient to support the use of neoadjuvant therapy as a routine approach for the management of pancreatic adenocarcinoma.

the current evidence supports the role of a multidisciplinary team in the management of pancreatic cancer and that the multidisciplinary team should be involved in all patients with pancreatic cancer, regardless of the stage of disease.
the current evidence does not support the use of the 3D CT in the preoperative evaluation of pancreatic head cancer, but the use of 2D CT is supported as the standard of care.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found that the presence of perineural invasion (PNI) on CT scan in patients with pancreatic cancer is a significant predictor for poor outcome.

we have developed a method to predict resectability of PDAC with multi-detector computed tomography (MDCT) that is highly accurate and reproducible, and has a strong correlation with surgical and pathologic findings.
the use of MDCT for the evaluation of pancreatic adenocarcinoma has improved the ability to determine the resectability of the tumor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a CT-based nomogram for the prediction of resectability of PDAC is a promising tool to help guide the surgical approach for patients with PDAC.
the majority of pancreatic cancer patients are not eligible for surgical resection.
the current standard of care for patients with pancreatic cancer is not optimal.
